curb_weight_kg.notes: Guide Auto lists 1,985 kg (4,376 lb) for the Canadian Preferred RWD (84.0 kWh); matches the US 2026 SE RWD (4,376 lb). Canadian spec relayed by a car guide, not read on Hyundai Canada.

Guide Auto lists 2,090 kg (4,608 lb) for the Canadian Preferred AWD on 19-inch wheels (matches US SE AWD 4,608 lb). The 20-inch (Ultimate Package) trim may weigh more; its figure was not found, so the value is for the 19-inch trim.

Converted from 4,707 lb (US XRT, CarFactSheet table attributed to Hyundai; EVSpecifications also gives 2,135 kg; KBB gives 4,720 lb = 2,141 kg). US figure; no Canadian XRT spec page found, assumed the same car (84 kWh, AWD).
Guide Auto lists 2,502 kg (5,516 lb) for the Canadian Essential RWD (110.3 kWh). US S RWD is 5,507 lb (2,498 kg, KBB), consistent.
Guide Auto lists 1,875 kg (4,134 lb) for the Canadian Light RWD (62.9 kWh); US Light is 4,132 lb (KBB). Page label may read "Weight"; presumed curb weight.
Guide Auto lists 1,995 kg (4,398 lb) for the Canadian Wind RWD (84.0 kWh).

Guide Auto lists "Weight" 2,100 kg (4,630 lb) for the Canadian Land AWD (84.0 kWh, P235/55R19); US Wind and GT-Line AWD are also 4,630 lb (KBB). Presumed curb weight; applies to the 19-inch trim, the 20-inch trim may differ.
Guide Auto lists 2,310 kg (5,093 lb) for the Canadian Light RWD (76.1 kWh).
Guide Auto lists "Weight" 2,418 kg (5,331 lb) for the Canadian Wind RWD (99.8 kWh); presumed curb weight.
Guide Auto lists 2,549 kg (5,620 lb) for the Canadian Land AWD (99.8 kWh; Guide Auto's tyre listing is P255/60R19, while our data lists 20-inch 275/50R20 for this trim).
Guide Auto lists 2,650 kg (5,842 lb) for the Canadian Land AWD with GT-Line Package (99.8 kWh, 21-inch). Page label may read "Weight"; presumed curb weight.

consumption_highway_wh_per_km.notes: Test: 75 mph (about 121 km/h) steady, temperature not stated, 21-inch 285/45R21 wheels (match this trim), battery-side vs wall-side not stated | Car and Driver 75-mph highway range test of the 2024 EV9 GT-Line AWD (99.8 kWh, same generation, pack, motors and wheels), 240 mi vs 270 mi EPA. 2.4 mi/kWh -> 1000 / (2.4 x 1.609344) = 259 Wh/km. Syndicated via AOL; original Car and Driver page not fetched. Not attached to other EV9 trims (19-inch wheels or different motors). Also seen: ArenaEV 130 km/h, 11 C, 33.2 kWh/100 km (332 Wh/km); outside 110-120 km/h so not used.

curb_weight_kg.notes: Guide Auto lists 2,684 kg (5,917 lb) for the Canadian 2026 EV9 GT (99.8 kWh, 21-inch).

Guide Auto lists "Weight" 1,688 kg (3,721 lb) for the Canadian 2026 Niro EV Wind (64.8 kWh, 17-inch); presumed curb weight. Other Canadian Niro EV trims may weigh slightly more; the variant has one trim.

consumption_highway_wh_per_km.notes: Test: ~75 mph (about 120 km/h) steady, ~14 C, dry, low wind, wheels not stated, battery-side vs wall-side not stated (article gives kWh per 100 km, probably car display) | InsideEVs 75 mph test of a Kona Electric Long Range (64.8 kWh, same generation and pack). Full-test figure 21.4 kWh per 100 km = 214 Wh/km (first 33 mi 20.3, midpoint 20.5 kWh/100 km). 132 mi driven with 18 % left. Test car was a 2024 (same generation and pack). Wind at his back on the first leg, against on the return.
